quote: A concept must have exactly one term inside a bounded context.
rule: Inside one component, each concept has one term across stories, ACs, business process, CDM, API and events.
check_hint: Compare the vocabulary of step 12b with CDM classes and API schemas; list concepts with more than one term.
notes: Synonym pairs from step 12b are the starting point.

quote: One term must not name two different concepts inside a bounded context.
rule: No term names two different concepts inside one component.
check_hint: Look for one term with two meanings across stories, API and CDM.

quote: The terms must be listed in a glossary per bounded context, with a one-line definition and the CDM class they map to.
rule: A glossary per component lists each term, a one-line definition and its CDM class.
check_hint: A glossary file exists; every CDM class and exposed API schema appears in it.
notes: Often missing in practice; step 23 drafts it.

quote: Status and other value sets must use the same values everywhere: the CDM, the API enum, the acceptance criteria and the UI labels.
rule: Status and value sets have the same values in the CDM, the API enums and the acceptance criteria.
check_hint: Compare enum values in the OpenAPI with CDM value sets and with status words in the ACs.

quote: If the UI shows a label that differs from the value, the mapping must be written down.
rule: A UI label that differs from the stored value has a written mapping.
check_hint: For each status shown in a UI story, find the value and the documented mapping.

quote: Every resource or schema an API exposes as a business object must map to a CDM entity or value object of the same name.
rule: Every business object an API exposes maps to a CDM entity or value object with the same name.
check_hint: Match OpenAPI schema names to CDM class names; list unmatched business schemas.
notes: Request and response wrappers are allowed (DDD-07).

quote: Request and response wrappers are allowed, but they must be recognisable as such and must not introduce a business concept the CDM lacks.
rule: API wrappers (requests, responses, pages, errors) do not introduce business concepts missing from the CDM.
check_hint: For each unmatched schema, decide wrapper or missing concept.

quote: Every attribute of an exposed business object should map to a CDM attribute of the same name.
rule: Each attribute of an exposed business object maps to a CDM attribute with the same name.
check_hint: Match schema properties to CDM attributes per matched class.

quote: the API must expose that identity under one name
rule: An entity's identity has one name in every API path, schema and event.
check_hint: Collect id-like parameters and properties per entity; flag different names.

quote: A value object (no identity of its own, compared by value) should not get its own id in the API.
rule: A value object has no id of its own in the API.
check_hint: Check CDM value objects against API schemas with an id field.
notes: Many CDMs do not mark value objects; step 23 flags it.

quote: Changes to an aggregate should go through its root
rule: Operations change an aggregate only through its root.
check_hint: For each write operation, name the aggregate root it acts on.

quote: An entity's lifecycle (its states and allowed transitions) must be defined once, in the CDM or next to it, and the API operations that change state must match those transitions.
rule: Each entity's states and transitions are defined once, and state-changing operations match them.
check_hint: Find the state set and transitions; map each state-changing operation and AC to a transition.

quote: Concepts owned by another bounded context must be marked as external in the CDM (`<<external>>`) and referenced by their owner's name and identity, not redefined.
rule: Concepts owned elsewhere are marked external in the CDM and not redefined.
check_hint: Classes with attributes that also appear as classes in another CDM; external classes without an owner.

quote: the translation must sit in one place (an anti-corruption layer), and the API of the component must use its own language, not the other context's.
rule: Translation to another context's model sits in one place, and the component's API uses its own language.
check_hint: Look for the other context's terms (for example EDC terms) in the component's API.

quote: The relations between contexts (who depends on whom, who owns which concept) should be shown in a context map.
rule: A context map shows the dependencies and concept ownership between components.
check_hint: A context map exists and agrees with the CDM external references.
notes: The CDM register's concept reference index would serve, but it is missing (17 Nov 2026).
